column1: # How a request's body value is written into its row, and how any JSON value the platform puts in a row is written (the
# canonical form): one table for the course (Source/tests/testdata/requests_body.tsv; w2cplatform/canonical.py) and the
# product (testdata/requests_body.tsv at its root; canonjson.go, requests.go), byte for byte. Owner: «Паритет».
# Rules: «Архитектор», 2026-10-05/06. The course's seed (2d517c88) merged in whole.
# THE STAND both tests file through: a family whose schema says `v: {maxLength: 32}` (a `request` row: POST /requests

# {"unit": <a unit>, "v": <body>}, the row's field `v` read back); and a table `counters` whose field `doc` is of type `json` (a `json` row: POST /counters {"name": …, "doc": <body>}, the unit's `doc` read back); a refusal is the 400's `fault`.
#     true / false      the JSON text: true, false (not Python's True)
#     null              at the top level of ANY field, a `json` one too: the field is ABSENT from the row (its default
#                       stands); an empty string is the empty string; inside a JSON value a null stays null
#     a number          exactly its digits, never through a float (Go: json.Number); a whole value in integer digits
#                       (5, not 5.0; -0 is 0); otherwise the shortest decimal that reads back as the same float, never
#                       an exponent; one past float64 (1e400) is refused: not_number
#     a string          as it is, unquoted, its own quotes its own; a string that looks like a number or a boolean
#                       stays the string; what type a field is, the schema says, not the text
#     length            the schema's maxLength over the WRITTEN text (1e40 is 41 digits: too_long); the writing
#   the canonical JSON — a dict or a list in a request row, and any value of a `json` field: compact, a dict's keys
#   sorted, UTF-8 as it is (no \u escaping; no HTML escaping of < > &; / not escaped), U+2028/2029 raw, control
#   characters as json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) writes them (\b \f \n \r \t short, the rest \u00xx lowercase),
#   numbers inside by the scalar rule, a null inside stays null. A `json` field's value is taken AS IT IS: a string
#   is a string document ("s" is stored "s"), never parsed again; the page parses its own text box before it sends,
#   its «not JSON» under the box (ADR-0002); not_json at a `json` field is only a body that is not JSON. Round trip:
#   the value read back and filed again is stored the same, byte for byte — both tests file every taken `json` row a
#   second time with the value they read. The ceiling of a `json` field: its canonical text's BYTES of UTF-8,
#   JSON_CEILING 4000: too_long. One function each side: canonical_json (course), CanonicalJSON (product).
#   ANY door of the platform: a body that is not UTF-8, holds a lone surrogate or a number past float64 is a 400 with
#   `fault` (not_json / not_number), its words those of fault.tsv (lesson 09).
#   not JSON is refused, never repaired: NaN, Infinity, a lone surrogate (\ud800) — not_json, not U+FFFD.
# Columns, tab-separated, one row a line; a line that begins with '#' and an empty line are no row:
#   field    request — the field `v` of a request row; json — the field `doc` of type json
#   body     the value as the body carries it, JSON text exactly as sent (5.0 is not 5)
#   stored   the text the row holds; <absent> — the field is not in the row; <empty> — the empty string
#   fault    empty (the tab is still there: every row has four columns) — taken; too_long — past the schema's maxLength (request) or JSON_CEILING (json);
#            not_number — a number past float64; not_json — a body that is not JSON
